I farm the same 10.1 mu in a wheat-maize rotation, so I will use the full 10.1 mu for winter wheat and then the same 10.1 mu again for summer maize. I have 20 years of experience, well irrigation, and some off-farm labor pressure in the family, so I will keep the plan practical and stable rather than complicated. For wheat, I will use improved seed, steady fertilizer, and a few irrigations because wheat in my area responds well to water and nitrogen, and I need reliable grain filling. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because it gives me the best yield on limited land, and I will keep fertilizer moderate but enough to support high output after wheat. I will use rotary tillage because it is efficient for my size of farm and fits the wheat-maize rotation well. I will control pests only as needed but I will not skip protection entirely, because one bad outbreak can cut yield quickly. My goal is dependable production and manageable labor, not taking unnecessary risks.
